metadata.description: Golden test cases for ShiftEase Time Engine
metadata.verification: All UTC values computed via Intl.DateTimeFormat (Node.js) against IANA tz database

expected.note: Spring-forward at 2:00 AM Mar 8: EST(UTC-5) -> EDT(UTC-4). 8h wall-clock = 7h actual.
Fall-back at 2:00 AM Nov 1: EDT(UTC-4) -> EST(UTC-5). 8h wall-clock = 9h actual.
2:30 AM does not exist on Mar 8 (clocks jump 2:00->3:00). Prompt user to choose interpretation.
1:00 AM occurs twice on Nov 1 (clocks fall 2:00->1:00). Prompt user to choose EDT or EST.
EU fall-back at 3:00 AM CEST(UTC+2) Oct 25 -> 2:00 AM CET(UTC+1). 8h wall-clock = 9h actual.
UK spring-forward at 1:00 AM Mar 29: GMT(UTC+0) -> BST(UTC+1). 8h wall-clock = 7h actual.
UK fall-back at 2:00 AM Oct 25: BST(UTC+1) -> GMT(UTC+0). 8h wall-clock = 9h actual.
AU spring-forward at 2:00 AM Oct 4: AEST(UTC+10) -> AEDT(UTC+11). 8h wall-clock = 7h actual. Proves code does not hardcode Northern Hemisphere DST months.
AU fall-back at 3:00 AM Apr 5: AEDT(UTC+11) -> AEST(UTC+10). 8h wall-clock = 9h actual. Proves Southern Hemisphere fall-back is in April, not October.
Normal overnight, no DST. Both in EST(UTC-5).
Year boundary, no DST. Both in EST(UTC-5).

cases.name: Regular 12h day shift (no DST, no overnight)

expected.note: Both in EDT(UTC-4). No DST transition.
Both in EDT(UTC-4). Overnight but no DST.

cases.name: Simple 8h daytime shift (no overnight, no DST)

expected.note: Simple 8h day shift, both in EDT(UTC-4).

cases.name: Existing occurrence keeps original timezone after device TZ change (INVARIANT-007)

expected.detail: Occurrence created with America/New_York must keep timezone=America/New_York even after user changes device to America/Los_Angeles. New occurrences from that point use America/Los_Angeles.
testSteps: Create occurrence with tz=America/New_York, shiftDate=2026-06-15, startTime=19:00, endTime=07:00+1
Create new occurrence with same pattern

cases.name: Recurrence basis stays local civil time across timezone changes (INVARIANT-003)

expected.detail: Pattern anchored at 19:00 local must always produce shifts starting at 19:00 local, regardless of timezone. When user moves from NY to London, the pattern still generates 19:00 London shifts (not 19:00 NY shifts displayed in London time).
testSteps: Generate occurrences: all start at 19:00 America/New_York
Verify existing occurrences still show 19:00 America/New_York
Generate new occurrences from pattern: they should use 19:00 America/New_York (pattern timezone, not device timezone)

expected.note: Very short shift crossing midnight. 2 minutes wall-clock = 2 minutes actual. Duration must be positive.

cases.name: Duration always from UTC instants, never from local subtraction (INVARIANT-002)

expected.detail: Local subtraction (06:00 - 22:00 + 24h = 8h) gives wrong answer. UTC-based calculation (10:00Z - 03:00Z = 7h) gives correct answer. Code MUST use UTC instants.

cases.name: Pattern projection cycle repetition property
cases.description: occurrence[n + cycleLengthDays] must have same templateId as occurrence[n]

testData.verification: For each index i, occurrence[i].templateId === occurrence[i + 8].templateId

cases.name: End time ambiguous (fall-back overlap) — D4 compliance

expected.note: 01:30 Nov 1 occurs twice in America/New_York (fall-back at 2:00 AM). Start time 23:30 Oct 31 is unambiguous (EDT/UTC-4). D4: end-time ambiguity must NOT be auto-resolved.

cases.name: Override isolation (INVARIANT-001): editing occurrence #N does not affect #N+1

testData.verification: After applying override at index 5, occurrences at indices 6, 7, 8, ... must be unchanged (same templateId, same UTC timestamps)

cases.name: Lord Howe fall-back 30-min DST (Australia/Lord_Howe) — ambiguous start

expected.note: Lord Howe DST is only 30 minutes (fall-back 2026-04-05 at 02:00 LHDT -> 01:30 LHST). 01:45 occurs twice; the 2 candidate UTC instants are exactly 30 minutes apart (14:45Z LHDT, 15:15Z LHST). The old +/-1h heuristic would have reported 60 minutes apart — WRONG. Proves DB-driven resolver handles 30-min DST zones.

cases.name: Lord Howe spring-forward 30-min DST — nonexistent start

expected.note: Lord Howe spring-forward 2026-10-04: clocks jump 02:00 LHDT -> 02:30 LHST (only 30 minutes). 02:15 falls inside the gap and does not exist at all. Offset candidate +10:30 maps naive 02:15 to 02:45 local; candidate +11:00 maps it to 01:45 local — neither round-trips to 02:15, so 0 candidates -> NONEXISTENT.

cases.name: Nonexistent calendar date (2026-02-31) is INVALID_DATE, not rollover, not DST

expected.note: DateTime.parse('2026-02-31') silently rolls to 2026-03-03 (probe E9). Strict round-trip validation must reject it as INVALID_DATE — never resolve it as a valid (different) day, and never classify it as a DST error.

cases.name: Time out of range (25:90) is INVALID_TIME, not rollover

expected.note: Hour > 23 and minute > 59 must be rejected as INVALID_TIME (hour 0..23, minute 0..59). A naive parse rolls 10:90 -> 11:30 silently.
M2: resolveShift previously returned a silent 0-duration success for 07:00->07:00. Now utcEnd <= utcStart is checked on RESOLVED UTC instants (INVARIANT-002), never local subtraction.

cases.name: Unknown timezone (Mars/Olympus) is INVALID_TIMEZONE, never NONEXISTENT

expected.note: D7/P0-8: an unknown IANA zone was previously caught by a catch-all and misreported as NONEXISTENT_LOCAL_TIME. tz.getLocation lookup failure must surface as INVALID_TIMEZONE, distinct from DST outcomes.

cases.name: Lord Howe regular shift in +10:30 offset (Australia/Lord_Howe)

expected.note: Lord Howe standard time is UTC+10:30 (half-hour offset). 08:00 local = 21:30Z previous day. Verifies the resolver and offset formatting keep half-hour precision (never offset.inHours which would truncate +10:30 to +10).
